title: Clarify context of §4.12.2 the `<noscript>` element
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Where §4.12.2 reads:

> [Contexts in which this element can be used](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-contexts):
>     In a [head](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-head-element) element of an [HTML document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document), if there are no ancestor [noscript](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-noscript-element) elements.
>     Where [phrasing content](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#phrasing-content-2) is expected in [HTML documents](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document), if there are no ancestor [noscript](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-noscript-element) elements.

Consider adding the following sentence:

> Where [flow content](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#flow-content-2) is expected in [HTML documents](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document), if there are no ancestor [noscript](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-noscript-element) elements.

Such a change would not only make the spec consistent with itself, but also [HTML 4.01](https://www.w3.org/TR/html401/sgml/dtd.html) and [XHTML 1](https://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-strict.dtd). See validator/validator#1694 for additional information.
